questions.question: What is a compact constructor in a record?
options: A constructor without a parameter list that validates values before assigning them
A constructor that accepts fewer parameters
A private constructor that only initializes final fields
A static method that creates the record
explanations: Correct. The compact constructor takes no parameters (they are defined in the record header) and is used to validate or transform values before assignment.
It does not refer to fewer parameters.
It is not a private constructor.
It is not a static method.

questions.question: Can instance fields be added to a record?
options: No, you can only have the fields defined in the record header
Yes, as many as needed
Only if they are static
Only if they are private
explanations: Correct. A record can only have the components (fields) declared in its header. It does not allow additional instance fields.
Instance fields cannot be added.
Static fields can be added, but they are not instance fields.
It is not a matter of visibility.

questions.question: Which interface do records implement?
options: They implement Serializable
They implement Comparable
They implement Iterable
They do not implement any interface
explanations: Correct. Records implement the Serializable interface, which allows them to be serialized.
They do not implement Comparable by default.
They do not implement Iterable by default.
They do implement at least Serializable.

questions.question: What is a record component?
options: Each parameter of the record, which becomes an immutable field
A private method of the record
A static constant of the record
An interface that the record implements
explanations: Correct. Each component (parameter in the header) becomes a final field with its accessor method (getter).
It is not a private method.
It is not a static constant.
It is not an interface.

questions.question: Can records extend other classes?
options: No, they inherit from java.lang.Record and cannot extend other classes
Yes, they can extend any class
They can only extend Object
They can only extend abstract classes
explanations: Correct. Records implicitly extend java.lang.Record and cannot extend other classes (Record in turn extends Object).
They cannot extend any class.
Object is Record's superclass, but it cannot be extended directly.
They are not limited to abstract classes.
